blind.B1: Yes. Human PBMC RNA-seq before and within 1 min after a 60-min single-leg knee-extension bout (S2.3.p1, S2.6.p1); all 30 libraries (15 participants x Pre/Post) carry the exercise factor. Age (Young n=7, Old n=8, S2.2.p1) is a second, non-exercise factor.
blind.B2: Young Post vs Pre (n=7 pairs, 14 samples; 53 DEGs, 52 up/1 down, of 13,695 genes, S3.2.p1); Old Post vs Pre (n=8 pairs, 16 samples; 1,026 DEGs, text 359 up/572 down, of 19,101 genes, S3.2.p1); baseline Old vs Young (665 DEGs, 446 up/199 down, of 19,762 genes, S3.1.p1; presumably Pre samples 8 vs 7).
blind.B3: Yes: each participant is sampled Pre and Post. Packet A key `subject` (S01..S19) appears once in each Pre/Post level and links 30/30 samples; the number is also in the GEO title.
blind.B4: Paper does not state the design formula. S4.2.p1 says 'the analyses were conducted separately for each age group' with different gene universes (13,695 vs 19,101), so separate per-group fits; whether pairing was modelled is not said (S2.7.p2 only gives DESeq2 1.40.2 + apeglm).
blind.B5: S2.8.p1: 'DEGs were identified using a threshold of p < 0.01, an adjusted p-value (FDR) of p < 0.01', then up and down genes split and only genes with log2FC greater than the group-specific mean kept for g:Profiler/IPA; Fig 1 legend colours DEGs by '>mean Log2 fold-change (p < 0.01)'. S2.7.p2 separately says 5% FDR. No fixed fold-change cutoff. Counts: 53 / 1,026 / 665 (26 shared up genes).

checks.evidence: Analyzed; matches B1 (S2.3.p1, DA.p1 names GSE293163; 30 libraries = 15 x 2).

packet B: Young 14 / Old 16 samples, Pre 15 / Post 15, subject x2; subsets Young 7 pairs, Old 8 pairs, Pre-only baseline 15 samples match S2.2.p1 and S3.2.p1. No exclusions. Baseline uses Pre samples, which the paper does not state explicitly but is the natural reading ('at baseline').
Post vs Pre (control Pre, treatment Post); Old vs Young (control Young). Young 97 up/2 down, SH2D3A down, as S3.2.p1; baseline Old more up than down as S3.1.p1.
Formula ~ subject + time within each age stratum; subject is categorical (S01.. recoded). Unpaired Young fit gives 0 DEGs, supporting paired fit as the paper's.
Separate per-age fits follow S4.2.p1; paper silent on pairing, both paired (primary) and unpaired (sensitivity) fits reported (execution records, young 99 vs 0, old 3613 vs 2274).

Sex is imbalanced (Young 2M/5F, Old 4M/4F, S2.2.p1) so the baseline Old vs Young contrast is partly sex-aliased; study caveats say 'No sex covariate available in GEO metadata' and 'associational', but the paper's own sex counts are not noted as a baseline confound. Within-person exercise contrasts are unaffected. Suitability sex check: pass, per-sex analysis possible.
checks.fix: Optionally add to the baseline caveat that Young/Old sex ratios differ (S2.2.p1).

checks.evidence: Integer featureCounts matrix (integer_fraction 1.0), DESeq2 route right. Low-count filter is CPM >= 0.4 in >=1 sample rather than the paper's read rule; tested genes Old 24,541 vs paper 19,101, baseline 21,665 vs 19,762 (Young 14,178 vs 13,695 close). Disclosed in deviations and HANDBACK.

padj < 0.01 transcribed from S2.8.p1, audit padj < 0.05 from S2.7.p2, conflict recorded. Paper's counts fit the post-hoc mean-log2FC subset better than the plain rule (packet B table; HANDBACK 44/1301/634 vs 53/1026/665); recorded as caveat/deviation, not silently used. Open policy question, not an error.

Comparison tables label the rule per column and the plain-rule counts (99/3613/1589) are not presented as matching. HANDBACK says the paper's counts 'match' the mean-LFC-subset counts, but 44 vs 53, 1,301 vs 1,026 and 634 vs 665 are not a match (Old 27% higher, up/down 376/925 vs 359/572); the study caveat's wording ('most likely') is more accurate.
checks.fix: Reword HANDBACK to 'are closer to' rather than 'match'.

checks.evidence: No stop or refusal in this case.

human_items: Which threshold to report when the paper's numbers fit the post-hoc mean-log2FC subset better than the stated FDR rule (open policy question).
summary: 该案例设计、配对、对比方向和模型拟合都与论文一致：按 subject 配对的年龄分层 Post vs Pre，另加基线 Old vs Young，并给出未配对敏感性分析。阈值冲突与论文计数差异已如实记录。仅有措辞层面的小问题（HANDBACK 将计数写成“匹配”、基线对比的性别失衡未注明），无阻断或重大问题。
